about.title: Loma Linda Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Loma Linda's economy is shaped heavily by its medical center and university, along with warehousing and retail near the I-10 corridor. Workers in these settings face injuries ranging from patient-handling strains to equipment accidents to slip-and-falls in busy facilities. In California, a workplace injury usually goes through the workers' compensation system first, since that system doesn't require proving employer fault. But when a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to the accident, a separate claim against that third party may also be possible. Our team handles both workers' compensation cases and third-party injury claims for workers in Loma Linda. If you were hurt while working in Loma Linda, we can review your case early to help you understand which paths are available to you and what deadlines apply.

whyChoose.title: Why Loma Linda Workers Choose Us

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires you to notify your employer of a workplace injury within 30 days. We can help make sure this step is handled correctly so your claim isn't jeopardized.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be pursued separately. We can evaluate whether this applies to your situation.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, we can advise you on your rights before you take any steps.

items.question: Do I have to go through workers' comp even if someone else caused my injury?
items.answer: In California, workers' compensation is typically the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault. However, if a third party — such as a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim against them. We can help determine if that applies to your case.

items.question: I was hurt at a Loma Linda hospital facility — does that change anything?
items.answer: Hospital and healthcare settings often involve subcontractors, medical equipment vendors, and outside maintenance companies, which can create third-party liability separate from workers' comp. Given how much of Loma Linda's workforce is tied to its medical campuses, this is worth having us review closely. Each situation depends on who was involved and what caused the injury.

items.question: What happens if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal under California law. If you experience demotion, reduced hours, or termination after reporting an injury, this may be a separate legal issue worth discussing with us. Documenting any changes in your employment after the injury can help support this.
